title: The Cat That Never Sleeps and the Bird That Wakes
text: That memory of mine begins on a certain day, I say. It was an unremarkable day when Father, as he did every morning back in the village, was tending to the monster stables as part of his daily routine. I, meanwhile, was over in the Filolial stables next door, thoroughly enjoying a refreshing morning of my own.
“Que… quee?”
“Que.”
Suddenly, the Filolial-samas began glancing restlessly around, their eyes darting this way and that, before all turning as one to face a single point. I wondered what on earth had happened.
“Naofumi-sama!”

Father had just stepped out of the monster stable when Big Sister called out with unusual urgency, so I too found myself stepping outside and heading toward where they were. The whole village had already been up and about, looking forward to breakfast, so everyone tilted their heads curiously at the sound of Big Sister’s voice and watched to see what was going on.
“Ah… seems we’ve got visitors,” Father muttered with a faint sigh, and set off walking with Big Sister at a rather sluggish pace.

“Ohh? Sounds like something’s up,” said Older Sister, who had apparently just gotten up despite having been drinking late into the night. Since she clearly wasn’t drunk, everyone around her began sensing danger in the air.
“Is there some kind of trouble? Shall I handle it, I say?”
“Motoyasu, you don’t need to do anything. It’s not really trouble, so just behave yourself.”
“Understood, I say!”

Father seemed to have already figured out what was going on. Looking for all the world like he was heading out on his morning stroll, Father walked ahead… and arrived at the village entrance. Da-da-da-da! The Filolial-samas all lined up together near the gate in an instant, while Rival, for whatever reason, was prostrate on the ground on the opposite side. And there, before them, stood… a rounded, cat-like Demi-Human standing about a hundred and thirty centimeters tall… alongside a bird-type monster, gleaming as though wreathed in crimson flame, sporting a long, peacock-like tail of feathers. Looking more closely at the cat Demi-Human, I noticed it had a fur-covered, lizard-like tail and was wearing overalls. Travelers passing through the neighboring town, perhaps? From somewhere around Siltvelt? But judging by the reactions of the Filolial-samas, Rival, and Big Sister, that clearly wasn’t it. Just what in the world was going on here, I wondered?
“Rival, what exactly are you doing, I say?”
“Shut up, nano! Rival doesn’t have time to deal with you right now! Be quiet, nano!”

Well, that was a strange reaction indeed. Oh! There, over there — that must be a big Filolial-sama! It looked like an ordinary Filolial, but nothing could fool these Motoyasu eyes! Just as I made to approach the large Filolial-sama, Ku, Marine, and Midori stopped me.
“No, Mokkun!”
“I don’t think you should upset that person!”
“Master, I have a feeling you really shouldn’t upset that person…”
Filo-tan too approached Father, pointing at the bird-type monster beside the cat Demi-Human in warning.
“You’re really putting them on edge, you know. Maybe tone it down a little?”
“Nah, nah, I’m not even giving off that much presence over here, am I? Ohh, this is a problem… I’m supposed to be the casual type, you know.”

And with that, in a manner that could only be described as royalty arriving incognito at some commoner’s doorstep, the cat Demi-Human and the bird monster seemed at a loss as to how to smooth things over.
“Ah, first off, everyone, don’t worry — I’m not the type to get upset over little things, so relax, take it easy. I really am just a visitor here, that’s all.”
The bird monster spread one wing out like a hand, addressing the Filolial-samas in reassurance. At that, the Filolial-samas seemed to relax just a little, the tension easing from their shoulders.

“Right, right, take it easy. Sorry for dropping by unannounced like this — we happened to run into an old friend nearby, and thought we’d swing by to say hello while making introductions. Figured the least we could do was greet you properly. Oh, and this bird here had something really good happen right before this, so it’s in a great mood — won’t get angry no matter what right now.”
“As long as your soul isn’t rotten, you can do whatever you want!”

The cat Demi-Human explained, pointing at the bird monster as it addressed Father. Did something happen if your soul was rotten? According to what Father had heard, there wasn’t anyone here with a rotten soul, apparently.
“And yet, despite that, both the dragon and the Filolials seem to be on high alert.”
“Raph…” Raph-chan, perched on Father’s shoulder, gave a little cry.
“Ah, that’d be this troublesome bird here. Being the progenitor of all winged creatures, it’s giving off this weird aura without holding back at all. Real nuisance, isn’t it?”
“Being popular is a heavy burden to bear… though you’re one to talk, leaking your own presence all over the place.”
“Mine’s fine because only certain people can even sense it. Otherwise they wouldn’t even notice, would they?”
“…If you could hide it, you should’ve just taken that thing down yourself. And what’s with the ‘I was alone’ bit, anyway?”
In response to Father, the cat Demi-Human answered with an easy, unbothered expression.

“The other side wasn’t quite that stupid, you know? Well, maybe a little stupid, actually. But yeah, I was alone that time. Not lying about that. Besides, you’re not the type to leave the fate of the world in someone else’s hands, are you?”
“Yeah, sure…”
The cat Demi-Human clapped its hands together with a pop, turning its gaze away from Father toward the rest of us standing behind him.
“Let me properly introduce myself, then. I suppose, from your perspective, I’d be what’s called a Godslayer. Name’s Ark. I had a little encounter with young Naofumi here, and lent him a hand.”
“That’s right.”
“Yes, we were saved that time.”

The cat Demi-Human, now introduced as Ark the Godslayer, spoke, and Father and the others nodded along. So then — this was someone Father owed a considerable debt to, in the matter of defeating the Crimson Swine’s true form. Father turned his gaze to the bird monster standing beside Ark.

“You’ve probably already heard from Ark, but I’m Naofumi Iwatani. This one here is Raphtalia. There’s a bunch more behind me too, but if we go through introductions one by one we’ll be here all day, so talk to whoever you like later if you want.”
“Sure, sure. My name is— well, like him, I’ve got a bunch of names, but I’m most often called the Phoenix, I guess? Though I’m not exactly immortal, mind you.”
“Well, folks who hunt down self-proclaimed gods being immortal would be something, huh.”
“That’s about the size of it. We just sort of… sleep and wake, that’s all.”
“I mean, that’s not really a name, is it?”

“I know, I know. Well, there’s ‘Phoenix’ too, and all that. You’ve got one of those in this world too, don’t you? So for simplicity’s sake here, just call me Ho — it’s close to what might end up being my next name anyway.”
So saying, the bird monster who called itself Ho gave a small bow.
“Oh, I’ve got a role as a Godslayer too, you know. Different from this one’s job of ending eternity, though.”
At the mention of “ending eternity,” Ho pointed at Ark. So there was that title as well, huh.
“Sometimes called the progenitor of all winged creatures too. World rebirth is his… job, but don’t worry. This world isn’t so old or rotten that it needs rebirthing.”
This all sounded like quite the grand scale of conversation — were these two on the same level as Ren or Black Thunder, perhaps?
“So you, being roughly on the same level as him, are what — the progenitor of dragons or something? You’ve got that kind of air about you.”
Father asked, looking over at Rival, who remained bowed low to the ground. So this was Rival’s point of origin, then! If that were the case, an enemy, I say!
“Hmm? Compared to the progenitor, I’d say I’m more like a sibling. The dragons just sort of consider me their boss, is all — it’s a bit different.”
“Sounds about the same to me.”
“Hmm… maybe think of it like an in-law sibling? Does that make more sense?”
No blood relation, but positioned as the sworn brother of the clan chief… I supposed I could picture that — definitely a slightly different position, I say.
“Haaah…” Father let out quite the weary sigh.
“Ah, you don’t need to look so troubled about it. It’d be a shame if you treated a visitor the way your world would with, what’s the phrase — serving bubuzuke tea as a hint to leave?”
A subtle way of saying “hurry up and go home,” I say. And to think, despite that appearance, it knew about Japanese customs!

“Well… I get it if you’re thinking ‘what now, took you long enough, you idiot!’ and feeling angry about it, but there are countless worlds out there, and it’s not like it’s fine — there were people actively preventing the warning signals from ever reaching us. Omniscience and omnipotence is nothing but arrogance anyway; it’s full of holes.”
Ark grumbled on rather thoroughly.
“While we’re staying here, I’ll at least let you vent your anger at me. You’ve more than earned that right. But, would you mind hearing our side of things, and the report, at least?”
“What is it?”
“The mastermind behind this whole affair — their world has already paid the price. No more waves will occur around here.”

Ark stated this flatly. Now that I thought of it, I’d just noticed — this person called Ark, I couldn’t sense a single thing from it, not even a trace of presence. Was this what being a Godslayer meant, I wondered?
“…I see.”
Father’s expression, which had remained flat through the report, finally softened with something like dissatisfaction.

“The one in charge tried making all sorts of excuses, but honestly, it was almost pathetic how they thought we wouldn’t dig deeper. That world had rotted through completely, root and branch. From their perspective, I’m probably nothing short of a mass murderer.”
Ark laughed as it said, “Well, whatever” — and for some reason, I felt like I’d seen that smile somewhere before.
“Anyway, that’s why we’ll be staying here a while, so take care of us.”
“Yeah, yeah. If you two are around, seems like troublesome sorts showing up will just resolve themselves without me lifting a finger. Just don’t slack off, though.”
“I know, I know. Gotta earn my keep somehow, right?”

Ho, having dismissed the Filolial-samas so they could relax and unwind as they pleased, joined back into the conversation. So then — the two Godslayers would be staying in the village for a while. The villagers, too, dispersed while chattering quietly among themselves. As for me, I wondered what to do — thinking of returning to my daily routine with the Filolial-samas — when Ho turned and looked at me.
“Ah, you — I recognize you. I remember now. You’re the one who made the news in that world I was in before, aren’t you? Motoyasu Kitamura, was it?”
“What? You know about Motoyasu?”

“I told you already, didn’t I? Before coming here, I spent some time in the world I was helping out — I remembered a little about him. Well, needless to say, he’s quite the celebrity. Woo-hoo, ladies’ man! Just like me!”

Father was glaring at me. Or rather, glaring at the spear more than me, it seemed. Something along the lines of: There was a Godslayer nearby and you didn’t even notice? Is your world really full of nothing but idiots like this? — I could practically feel Father’s thoughts radiating toward me.
“I-I don’t know anything about it, I say!”
“Well, no surprise you wouldn’t recognize me from back then. There was a lot going on with me at the time, you know. I’m all shining and glorious now, though!”

Seemed there was some kind of reason behind it. I didn’t know the particulars of Ho’s circumstances, but I was saved nonetheless, I say. Still, its sense of humor was… a touch cringeworthy. It felt a bit like watching my past self, giving me an itchy, uncomfortable feeling.
“…The news, huh.”

“Yep. Story was that he got killed in some crime-of-passion mess, but he ended up summoned to this world and avoided death that way… still some lingering traces of causal interference from this whole affair’s mastermind. I see, I see. Because he was killed, apparently all sorts of related parties went on a rampage, and the culprit met a rather gruesome end. Something about university— oop, that’s edging into someone’s privacy, not really my place to talk about it. Sorry ’bout that.”
So Ho seemed to be talking about matters related to my original world. Terribly irrelevant stuff, honestly.

“Oh? Trying to use his inherent nature to avoid ruin in an emergency, huh. I see, I see. Pure coincidence, but the fact that you and we ended up in the same world might’ve been some kind of causal connection after all.”
“Causal, I say?”
“Yep. Well, it’s something like your own nature, I suppose.”
This Ho person was saying things I couldn’t quite make sense of at all.

“…So Motoyasu, huh. Well, sounds like his ex from back home met a tragic end. Attempted murder-suicide, was it… no wait, if it was supposed to be a murder-suicide, but she still faced consequences… why is that?”
“Ended up too attached to her own life to go through with dying, in the end?”
“Pigs value their own hides above all else, I say. Drunk on the emotion of claiming to love me, no doubt, and once I was dead, it fled back to save its own precious self, I say.”
Pigs truly are a menace, I say! Ptooey! Indeed, I say!

“Well… even with some degree of interference, that particular part of a person doesn’t really change. She was pulled out of all those messy entanglements and summoned to this world instead — I’d say that actually worked out for the best, wouldn’t you?”
“…Motoyasu, do you have any wish to go back to your original world?”
“None whatsoever, I say. A world without Filo-tan and Filolial-sama holds no value at all, I say!”
“…There you have it. Good for you. Bird boss, I’d bet you’re about to become an object of worship for this guy too.”
“Ehh… you’re going to worship me? I get uncomfortable if people expect weird returns for that sort of thing, you know? Happens more often than you’d think.”
Was Ho a Filolial-sama or not, I wondered? I approached Ho to conduct my judgment. Sniff, sniff, I say.
“Wh-what are you doing?”

Hmm… somehow, it did seem to carry that same rich, fragrant scent found in Filolial-samas. …Though, now that I thought about it, it also somewhat resembled the scent I recalled from when we defeated the Phoenix. In that sense, the description of “boss of the Filolial-samas” wasn’t inaccurate at all. Phoenix… now that I thought of it, the actual Phoenix had shared similar characteristics too. That made sense, I say.

“Right then, Ho, was it. I hereby acknowledge you as a Filolial-sama, I say! Rest assured — I seek no returns whatsoever from a Filolial-sama, I say! From this day forth, you shall be Ho-kun. I shall love Ho-kun equally alongside all the rest, I say.”
“Hold on a second! Please don’t lump me in with a bunch who consider pulling carts the highest form of joy in life!?”
Here, Ho pointed accusingly at the cart-pulling Filolial-sama in protest!
“What manner of blasphemy is this, I say! The Filolial-sama who pulls the cart is the very pinnacle of existence, I say! Ho-kun! You simply haven’t noticed that instinct within yourself yet, I say!”
“No, no, no, absolutely not! If you try to make me pull a cart, I will get angry, you hear me!?”
The Filolial-samas watched Ho’s refusal of my proposal with what seemed to be genuine concern. There was no need to worry so — no Filolial-sama could truly resist their own instincts, I say.
“Motoyasu doesn’t get angry even at insults that seem to deny Filolials, so long as he’s already decided to accept the thing, huh.”
“I suppose you could call it thoroughness, or something like that…”
“Well, it’s exceedingly troublesome, but maybe that’s a good quality too, in its own way.”
In any case, it seemed the apparent boss of the Filolial-samas would be staying in the village for a while, I say.
“…In any case, seems Filolials as a species have a nature that makes them want to avoid trouble. Watching their boss warily from a distance, I suppose.”
“Seems that way.”
“So, about Ark, boss of the dragons…”
Father looked around and turned toward Ark, who was smiling pleasantly nearby.
“You said you’re a visitor here… any particular plans for what you’ll be doing?”

“Just came to deliver the report on the incident and introduce you to this troublesome bird here — no particular plans beyond that. Oh, but if there’s work you’d like done, I don’t mind helping, so just say the word.”

“Managing the territory… looks like you’ve got a lot going on. This cat-slash-dragon guy, you know, does dorm-mother type work and childcare stuff on a whim sometimes — pretty useful, actually. Since he’s offering, might as well put him to work.”
Ho pointed at Ark, explaining to Father. Dorm mother and childcare, was it? So this meant a high aptitude for housework and childrearing, then.
“Ahh, brings back memories.”
“Hoh… well then, might as well have you help with various things.”
“Sounds fine to me.”
As this conversation went on, Rival watched from a distance, brows furrowed.
“Whoa… it’s looking at you like you just proposed something terrifying. Like, ‘Aren’t you scared, putting a Godslayer who’s also the dragon boss to menial chores?’ sort of look.”
“Don’t worry about it. Isn’t it worse if we’re not allowed to do anything and just get treated as honored guests?”
“Yeah, fair. Feels like there’s some hidden catch to that, doesn’t it.”
I see. Having power or authority tends to invite suspicion, doesn’t it. Ho and the others must have had their own struggles too, then. Seemed even Godslayers had their fair share of troubles.
“So… Ho, what exactly can you do?”
“Hm? Want me to whip up some fried rice with my flames?”
“Motoyasu can handle that much just fine.”

“Oh really? I think my fried rice is pretty good, though… well, I can do plenty of things, not that I can’t, but maybe wait until you’ve got a full picture of what’s needed before deciding? Oh, and I don’t do any secret techniques or prophecy-type stuff, just so you know.”
“Wasn’t expecting any of that from the start, honestly… what kind of preemptive excuse is that supposed to be. Anyway, I was in the middle of preparing breakfast. If you can cook, help out.”
When Father requested Ark’s help, it nodded in response.
“Guess I’ll help out then. First, let’s figure out what kind of flavors people like around here.”

And with that, Ark rolled up its sleeves and headed off toward the kitchen with Father. So the two of them cooked together in the kitchen. Father, looking rather bothered, cut ingredients midair with careless efficiency.
“So this is the kind of flavor that’s popular here, huh — alright, this should work.”
Ark too, in the kitchen, sampled the simmering pot with practiced ease, helping with the stewing. It casually pinched seasoning between its fingers and tossed it in without a second thought.
“Ah, Naofumi-kun. Pass me some of that ingredient there.”
“Sure. Toss me some of what you’re cutting too.”
“Yeah.”

Tap! Father sent the ingredients he’d cut flying with practiced skill toward Ark, and Ark tossed them back with a similarly deft motion. The village’s kitchen assistants watched, dumbfounded, at the sight. Father and Ark were cooking in perfect sync, exchanging ingredients back and forth. There was no room to step in between them, I say — jump in carelessly and you’d likely get hit by flying ingredients from both directions. This wasn’t on the level of mere “practiced hands,” I say. I could see now what Ho meant about the dorm-mother business. And so, before long, the cooking was finished and breakfast was set out before us.
“Bro, the food’s amazing again today! Which one’s the dish Ark-san made?”
“This one right here.”

When Keel asked, Ark had apparently made the soup. It fell short of Father’s slow-simmered, all-night soup, but personally, I thought it tasted quite good, I say. A somewhat richer flavor, more suited to modern tastes.
“Ohh! So this is the one Ark-san made!”
“That’s right. Haven’t quite matched it to the local flavors yet, though. If anything, it’s seasoned more for you modern folks — Naofumi-kun and the rest — rather than for the local palate.”
“Well, if you’re asking about my personal preference, this one’s spot on. Fairly versatile seasoning, I’d say.”

“Cooking’s all about individual preference, after all. Adjusting it to match the person eating is half the fun of it… but if you suddenly serve exactly what someone likes right off the bat, wouldn’t that kind of freak them out?”
“…Yeah, true enough.”

Father agreed with Ark’s remark. Indeed, Father was quite skilled at recreating flavors he already knew. Apparently he understood that if he immediately achieved a perfect recreation on the first try, it might come across as unsettling.
“Dunno exactly what’s going on, but this is tasty in its own way!”
Keel munched away, commenting on the food Father and the others had made.
“Hey, hey, Ark-san, you travel all over fighting off bad guys who show up in this world and stuff, right?”
“I suppose that’s how it’d look from your perspective.”
“So tell us about your travels!”
Keel asked Ark with remarkable familiarity.
“Hold on a sec — what about me!? I travel too, you know!”
Ho-kun asserted itself at this point.
“The journey… of life, you mean.”
“You’re a bird.”
Father and Ark looked at Ho-kun with the exact same expression. Their faces practically read “what an annoying creature.” Well then, allow me to ask instead.
“Ho-kun, tell me all about it, I say!”
